text:
### Observed differences

- The choice of route after A05 shifted. In the earlier window, A05 was followed by A01 in about 39 of 100 of its outgoing transitions, by A10 in about 25 and by A11 in about 26; in the later window, A01 took about 49 of 100, while A10 fell to about 21 and A11 to about 23. [DIR002]
- Participation moved in mirror image: A01 appeared in 46% of traces before versus about 53% in the later window (92 vs 105 of 200 traces), while A10 and A11 each dropped from 54% to about 48% (108 vs 95 traces). [OCC001, OCC008, OCC009]
- A01 on one side and A10/A11 on the other are strict alternatives: they never share a trace in either window (co-occurrence zero, shares summing to 100%), so the gain of A01 equals the loss of the A10/A11 route one-for-one. A10 and A11 still occur together in about half of the traces (54% vs 47.5%), in either order, and both still lead on to A07. [REL009, REL010, REL055, DIR004, DIR005]
- The surrounding structure is stable: A05 and A07 still occur in every trace in both windows, A01 is still immediately followed by A07 in about 95–96% of its occurrences in both windows, and A05 still precedes A01 in the large majority of joint appearances (about 85% before, 93% after). [POS002, POS003, DIR001, LAG006, REL004, REL006]
- Positions and distances move exactly as this branch shift predicts: A07's median position moved from 0.75 to 0.667 (a difference exceeded in only about 3 of 100 random re-splits), and the A05→A07 distance shifted from roughly half lag-2 / half lag-3 towards lag-2 — the pattern expected when a larger share of traces takes the shorter A01 route. [POS003, LAG012]
- Smaller shifts in the segment after A07: A02 doubled from about 4.5% to 9% of traces (9 vs 18 traces) and its share of A07's outgoing transitions rose from 4.5% to 9%; A06 fell from about 14.5% to 9.5% of traces (29 vs 19); A03 slipped from 29.5% to 26.5% while A04 (21.5% → 24%) and A08 (24.5% → 26%) edged up. [OCC002, OCC005, DIR003, OCC003, OCC004, OCC006]
- The reversed order A01 before A05 became rarer: 14 traces before versus 7 after, and A07 was followed by A05 in 7.5% versus 3% of its outgoing transitions. [REL004, LAG004, DIR003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that two existing alternative paths after A05 were taken with different frequencies. In the earlier window, roughly 46 of 100 cases ran A05 → A01 → A07 (A01 almost always immediately followed by A07) and roughly 54 of 100 ran through A10 and A11, which execute together adjacently in either order before reaching A07; in the later window this split moved to about 53 versus 48 of 100. All involved activities (A05, A01, A10, A11, A07) are observed in substantial shares in both windows, A01 still never co-occurs with A10/A11, A05 and A07 still appear in every trace, and no activity started or stopped repeating, so this reads as a redistribution of traffic between existing alternatives rather than paths or activities being added or removed. [DIR002, OCC001, OCC008, OCC009, REL009, REL010, REL055, REL006, POS002, POS003]

The change is visible directly at the branching point A05, is mirrored one-for-one in participation and in the A01-versus-A10/A11 relation, and is independently reflected in A07's position distribution and the A05→A07 lag mix, which shift by the amounts the new branch shares predict; the A01→A07 succession itself is essentially unchanged, consistent with a share shift rather than a structural rewiring. [DIR002, REL009, REL010, POS003, LAG012, DIR001, LAG006]

Limitations: the windows are finite 200-trace samples and the evidence carries no screening baseline, so the number of qualifying items cannot be compared with a chance expectation; individually, the routing and participation differences are exceeded in roughly 2 of 10 random re-splits, so a sampling artefact of the two windows remains a competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out, and the agreeing items partly describe the same traces rather than confirming independently. [DIR002, OCC001, OCC008, OCC009]

Other differences: after A07, A02 was executed in about 9 of 100 traces versus about 4.5 before (9 vs 18 traces) and A06 in about 9.5 versus 14.5 (19 vs 29 traces), with smaller movements for A03, A04 and A08 — all based on few observations and kept out of the main hypothesis [OCC002, OCC005, DIR003, OCC003, OCC004, OCC006]; the reversed order A01 before A05 also halved (7 vs 14 traces) [REL004, LAG004].
